title: Valuation Desk Memorandum: The Grade Deduction Taken from the Registration's Own Entries
content:
The deduction made to a valuation under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes for the condition of the traded piece is the deduction the desk publishes for the grade the registration's entries record. The grade the entries record stands over any grade carried elsewhere on the file.

## The memorandum

Six percent (6 percent) is deducted where an inspection stands among the registration's entries and the later of them grades the piece good. Twenty percent (20 percent) is deducted where an inspection stands among them and the later of them grades the piece fair. Nothing is deducted where no inspection stands among them or they grade it otherwise.

An inspection stands among the entries where an inspection entry is recorded against the registration; where several stand, the grade recorded on the later of them governs.

## By grade recorded

| Inspection among the registration's entries | Grade on the later inspection | Deduction |
|---|---|---|
| yes | good | 6 percent |
| yes | fair | 20 percent |
| yes | excellent | nothing |
| yes | damaged | nothing |
| yes | any other grade | nothing |
| no | — | nothing |

## Readings on a figure of 10000 USD

- Later inspection grades the piece good: 6 percent is deducted, leaving 9400.00 USD.
- Later inspection grades the piece fair: 20 percent is deducted, leaving 8000.00 USD.
- Two inspections stand, the earlier grading the piece fair and the later good: the later governs, so 6 percent is deducted and 9400.00 USD remains.
- No inspection entry stands: nothing is deducted, and 10000.00 USD remains.
